answer.summary: Nikita Miller replaces the ideal of constant “balance” with optimizing for what matters at a given time, accepting that not everything can receive equal attention all the time. She finds it healthier to let work and personal priorities shift across periods and life stages.

sections.heading: Optimize for the moment, not perfect balance
sections.content: Miller says she thinks in terms of “optimization”: ask what you are optimizing for today, this quarter, or this year, while recognizing you cannot have it all at once. Earlier in her career, she sometimes worked long hours around product releases; when training for a race, she might instead take a long morning run and start work at 10 a.m. Now, she may choose particular weeks or days to handle her children’s drop-offs and pickups. She says this shifting approach feels healthier than expecting everything to be equally well cared for all the time.

sections.heading: Make choices that fit your life stage
sections.content: She also sees these trade-offs as dependent on where you are in life. For example, she says that at her current stage she probably would not choose a very early-stage startup, because she believes that role may require being in person and working long hours together. That is her personal choice, not a universal rule.
